title: 2010 HMMT November Guts Problem 15
statement: Distinct points \(A, B, C, D\) are given such that triangles \(A B C\) and \(A B D\) are equilateral and both are of side length 10 . Point \(E\) lies inside triangle \(A B C\) such that \(E A=8\) and \(E B=3\), and point \(F\) lies inside triangle \(A B D\) such that \(F D=8\) and \(F B=3\). What is the area of quadrilateral \(A E F D\) ?

solutions.text: \(\frac{\frac{91 \sqrt{3}}{4}}{}\) Since \(A E B \cong D F B\), we have \(\angle E B A=\angle F B D\). Thus, \(\angle E B F=\angle E B A+\angle A B F=\) \(\angle F B D+\angle A B F=\angle A B D=60^{\circ}\). Since \(E B=B F=3\), this means that \(E B F\) is an equilateral triangle of side length 3. Now we have \([A E F D]=[A E B D]-[E B F]-[F B D]=[A E B]+[A B D]-[E B F]-\) \([F B D]=[A B D]-[E B F]=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\left(10^{2}-3^{2}\right)=\frac{91 \sqrt{3}}{4}\).
